applies_why: The judge text uses an UNDERDETERMINED label on a Matthew 1:20 single-verse issue while noting both the challenger's footed analogy and the verse's own stated source, so it treats the verse's senses as open rather than settling them under K-S2.
quote: D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb; answered in [CR3] LINK 2.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand. I weighed reading one, that a two-sense verse cannot be UNDERDETERMINED and both senses count, against reading two, that the clause only bars calling the verse open when both senses are explicitly present, so an UNDERDETERMINED label could still stand.
why: The judge labels the Matthew 1:20 issue UNDERDETERMINED even though the rule says a two-sense verse is not open and both senses stand, so the text breaches K-S2.
